bibl.title: Stochastic Variational Inference
bibl.publisher: Journal of Machine Learning Research / arXiv

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We develop stochastic variational inference, a scalable algorithm for approximating posterior distributions.

span.label: scalable approximate posterior inference in hierarchical Bayesian models
span.quote: Inference algorithms of the 1990s and 2000s used to be considered scalable, but they cannot easily handle the amount of data that we described in the four examples above.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We develop this technique for a large class of probabilistic models and we demonstrate it with two probabilistic topic models, latent Dirichlet allocation and the hierarchical Dirichlet process topic model.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THREE SOURCES FOR A MODEL'S ASSUMPTIONS ARE NAMED, AND WHAT THEY ASSERT IS DECLARED UNOBSERVABLE IN THE SAME CLAUSE: we have assumptions to make - FROM SCIENCE, INTUITION, OR OTHER DATA ANALYSES - that involve STRUCTURES WE BELIEVE EXIST IN THE DATA BUT THAT WE CANNOT DIRECTLY OBSERVE. The provenance of the assumptions and the inaccessibility of their objects are stated together
span.quote: Our data are complex and high-dimensional; we have assumptions to make—from science, intuition, or other data analyses—that involve structures we believe exist in the data but that we cannot directly observe; and finally our data sets are large, possibly even arriving in a never-ending stream.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A FORMALISM IS DESCRIBED AS A LANGUAGE, AND THE INFERENCE PROCEDURE AS ITS READING: probabilistic graphical models GIVE US A VISUAL LANGUAGE FOR EXPRESSING ASSUMPTIONS about data and its HIDDEN STRUCTURE, and the corresponding algorithms LET US ANALYZE DATA UNDER THOSE ASSUMPTIONS, INFERRING THE HIDDEN STRUCTURE THAT BEST EXPLAINS OUR OBSERVATIONS. The notation is cast as a vocabulary and the computation as its interpretation
span.quote: In particular, probabilistic graphical models give us a visual language for expressing assumptions about data and its hidden structure. The corresponding posterior inference algorithms let us analyze data under those assumptions, inferring the hidden structure that best explains our observations.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE PAPER'S OWN TASKS ARE SPLIT INTO TWO KINDS WITH DIFFERENT WARRANTS, AND THE UNOBSERVED PART IS PUT IN SCARE QUOTES: in DESCRIPTIVE tasks the models help EXPLORE the data with the hidden structure probabilistically FILLED IN; in PREDICTIVE tasks they FORM PREDICTIONS ABOUT NEW OBSERVATIONS. The same machinery serves two purposes that would be judged by different evidence
span.quote: In descriptive tasks, like problems #1 and #4 above, graphical models help us explore the data— the organization of books or the connections between genes and traits—with the hidden structure probabilistically “filled in.” In predictive tasks, like problems #2 and #3, we use models to form predictions about new observations. For example, we can make recommendations to users or predict the class labels of new images.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A MODEL CLASS IS DEFINED BY WHAT IT COSTS RATHER THAN BY WHAT IT CONTAINS: NONCONJUGATE MODELS are MODELS WHERE A RICHER PRIOR IS USED AT THE EXPENSE OF MATHEMATICAL CONVENIENCE - and they HAVE EXPANDED THE SUITE of tools available. The category's definition is a trade-off, with the thing traded away named explicitly
span.quote: This class of models is expressive, but nonconjugate models—models where a richer prior is used at the expense of mathematical convenience—have expanded the suite of probabilistic tools at our disposal.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: ONE ALGORITHM IS RE-DESCRIBED AS ANOTHER, AND THE EQUIVALENCE IS STATED AS AN IDENTITY OF STEPS: the classical coordinate ascent algorithm CAN THUS BE INTERPRETED AS a projected natural gradient algorithm - and updating a parameter by taking a natural gradient step OF LENGTH ONE IS EQUIVALENT TO PERFORMING A COORDINATE UPDATE. Two names for one procedure, with the exchange rate given
span.quote: The classical coordinate ascent algorithm can thus be interpreted as a projected natural gradient algorithm (Sato, 2001). Updating a parameter by taking a natural gradient step of length one is equivalent to performing a coordinate update.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A FORMAL FACT IS GIVEN AN INTUITIVE ROUTE ALONGSIDE THE FORMAL ONE, AND BOTH ARE LABELLED: FORMALLY this is most easily seen via other perspectives, THOUGH IT CAN BE SEEN INTUITIVELY WITH the stick-breaking construction - and then THE INTUITION IS THAT more of the stick is absorbed in the first break locations. The paper marks which of its two explanations is which
span.quote: Formally, this is most easily seen via other perspectives on the DP (Ferguson, 1973; Blackwell and MacQueen, 1973; Pitman, 2002), though it can be seen intuitively with the stick-breaking construction. The intuition is that as α gets smaller more of the stick is absorbed in the first break locations

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE EVALUATION CRITERION IS OPERATIONALISED AS A PROBABILITY ASSIGNED TO WITHHELD WORDS: under the predictive distribution, A BETTER MODEL WILL ASSIGN HIGHER PROBABILITY TO THE HELD-OUT WORDS - and the procedure divides each document into observed and held-out words, KEEPING THE SETS OF UNIQUE WORDS DISJOINT. What BETTER means is fixed by a number and a partition, and the partition rule is stated
span.quote: Under this predictive distribution, a better model will assign higher probability to the held-out words. In more detail, we divide each test document’s words w into a set of observed words wobs and held-out words who, keeping the sets of unique words in wobs and who disjoint.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PROCEDURE IS NAMED BY COMPOSING TWO EXISTING NAMES: interleaving the coordinate ascent updates with an update that increases the bound IS CALLED VARIATIONAL EXPECTATION-MAXIMIZATION - and the stochastic version is then described by what it does DIFFERENTLY, updating the two simultaneously. The name records its parentage and the variant is defined against it
span.quote: In the non-stochastic setting, α can be optimized by interleaving the coordinate ascent updates in Figure 3 with an update for α that increases the ELBO. This is called variational expectation-maximization.

span.label: The general algorithm is derived only for conjugate exponential-family models and does not cover nonconjugate models such as correlated or dynamic topic models.
span.quote: We developed our algorithm with conjugate exponential family models.

span.label: Convergence is only to a local optimum, and very small minibatches can lead to a poor one.
span.quote: Stochastic variational inference is guaranteed to converge to a local optimum but taking large steps on the basis of very few data points may lead to a poor one.

span.label: The quality of the solution and speed of convergence depend on how the forgetting rate, delay and minibatch size are set.
span.quote: Although stochastic variational inference algorithm converges to a stationary point for any valid κ, τ , and S, the quality of this stationary point and the speed of convergence may depend on how these parameters are set.

span.label: What is optimised is a bound standing in for a quantity the method cannot compute.
span.quote: Since we cannot compute p(x | α) exactly, an approximate approach is to maximize the fitted variational lower bound

span.label: A prior is made exchangeable for simplicity, and the paper notes the conditional then is not.
span.quote: but for simplicity we assume exchangeable Dirichlet priors; that is, we require that all of these parameters are set to the same value

span.label: The evaluation is built from a split of each test document's words, constructed to be disjoint.
span.quote: we divide each test document’s words w into a set of observed words wobs and held-out words who, keeping the sets of unique words in wobs and who disjoint

span.label: How many topics a collection needs is answered by the model's own posterior.
span.quote: Given a collection of documents, the posterior distribution of the hidden structure determines how many topics are needed to describe them

span.label: a topic - A WEIGHTED DISTRIBUTION OVER THE VOCABULARY: not a subject, a theme or an aboutness, but a probability vector over words, shown to a reader by printing its most frequent members - which is why a multi-word name has no way to stay together inside one
span.quote: Each topic is a weighted distribution over the vocabulary and each topic’s plot illustrates its most frequent words

span.label: the ELBO - A LOWER BOUND SUBSTITUTED FOR THE THING WANTED: the algorithm maximises a bound on the log marginal probability rather than that probability, and the gap between them is not reported because computing it would require the quantity the bound exists to avoid
span.quote: It maximizes the evidence lower bound (ELBO), a lower bound on the logarithm of the marginal probability of the observations
